answer: Sybil resistance makes coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities sign conflicting messages, pairwise evidence triggers penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, hence O(k²), rather than a flat per-node fine. Bonded escrows and asymmetric depreciation compound losses on detected swarm capital, producing an exponential multiplier as exposure grows; splitting one operator across names does not dilute liability. The fable of a ferrous key on a terrace is only an analogy, not a protocol assumption.
